column7: control (S3-F1 with a big literal): b' = (fun n => (g n h).1) N is ANOTHER term than b = (g N h).1 although it reduces to it: no pair of m_success answers, the cheap whnf_core of a is 5: false

literals are compared BY VALUE in term identity: b = (g N h).1 and b' = (g N' h).1 with N, N' two natVal records of the same number above 2^64. Officially one term: m_success answers W2. A store with one node per literal RECORD has two terms and rejects
the same with the binder info (default / implicit) instead of the name
binder names in a DEFINITION (no sharecommon: the two lambdas are two objects, structurally equal)

binder names are NOT part of the official term identity (expr_eq_fn<false>): b = (f ((fun (x : A) => x) h)).1, b' the same with the binder called y (another record). Officially (a = a, a = b') is the pair (a = a, a = b): m_success answers W2
the same in a DEFINITION (the official reader makes two objects, no sharecommon)
two export records with the same content are ONE term for the official caches (structural keys): b' is a copy of b in which every record is new. m_success answers W2

let nondep is part of the official term identity (expr_eq_fn: let_nondep(a) == let_nondep(b); the hash is the same). W = use (a = L) (Eq.refl a) with L = (let x : Nat := 0; b) nondep = false, W0, W2 = use (a = L2) (Eq.refl a) with L2 the same let with nondep = true. Officially (a = a, a = L2) and (a, L2) are new pairs, the cheap whnf_core of a answers 5: false. A store that does not keep the flag has ONE term for L and L2 and answers W2 from the success cache
the same as r2-id-let-nondep-bad in a DEFINITION (add_definition does not run sharecommon on the value)
twin: without W0 (the cache stays empty)
control: W2 repeats the let with the SAME flag (nondep = true in both): one term, answered by m_success
the same with b' = (f.{imax 0 0} h).1

levels are compared STRUCTURALLY in term identity: b = (f.{0} h).1, b' = (f.{max 0 0} h).1. Officially b' is another term: no pair of m_success answers, the cheap whnf_core of a is 5: false. A store that normalises levels at load (max 0 0 = 0) has one term and accepts
twin: without W0

a literal and its constructor form are two terms: b = (g 7 h).1, b' = (g (Nat.succ 6) h).1. Officially no pair answers (the arguments 7 and Nat.succ 6 would be equal, but the cheap whnf_core of a is 5 before g is looked at): false
the same with a literal below 2^64 (7)
control: W2 = needs c0 alone (U = U' in an empty cache)

object identity, is_eqp(t_n_n, t_n) in is_def_eq_core: cX := X and cS := Nat.succ X' with X' ANOTHER RECORD with the content of X = S.q.1. The full whnf_core of X' (Nat folding of Nat.succ X') writes the m_whnf_core entry; the second whnf_core(X) is answered with the object X', which is not X: is_def_eq_core runs once more on (X', Nat.succ X'), its proof-irrelevance step infers the type c0 of X' and asks is_prop(c0), which caches the full whnf_core of U = (F intro).1; W2 = needs c0 then compares U with U' = (F h).1 and the cheap whnf_core of U is Type: false. An engine with one id for X and X' has no second pass
r2-ptr-other-record-bad with a DEFINITION as the checked declaration
control: the other record, W2 before W1 (U and U' are compared before anything is cached)
r2-ptr-same-record-ok with a DEFINITION as the checked declaration

twin, THE SAME TERMS: cS := Nat.succ X with the SAME record as the value of cX. One object: the entry is written by X itself, no second pass, U has no entry, U = U' holds (lazy_delta_proj_reduction: F intro against F h, proof irrelevance)

whnf_core cache against the POS pair table, ONE theorem, v0: W = use (a = b) (Eq.refl a) (true while the cache is empty; the official m_success holds the TERM pair (a, b)), then W0 = use (a = 5) (Eq.refl 5) (full whnf_core of a = (f intro).1 cached: 5), then W2 = use (a = mdata b) (Eq.refl a): officially a new term pair, the cheap whnf_core of a is answered 5 by the cache and 5 against (f h).1 is false. An engine whose pair table is keyed by VALUES (mdata is transparent) answers the POS pair of W
twin: without the middle argument (the cache stays empty)

mdata hides eagerReduce from the official is_eager_reduce (get_app_fn of an mdata node is the node): the argument mdata (eagerReduce (X = X) (Eq.refl X)) is compared in PLAIN mode, where X = Y p is true (package S, S-F5: eager false). An engine that drops mdata enters eager reduction

whnf_core cache, base: (f intro).1 = (f h).1 by Eq.refl ((f intro).1), f x := S.B.mk (And.rec (fun _ _ => 5) x) regular. Both sides are stuck projections for the cheap whnf_core, lazy_delta_proj_reduction compares f intro with f h: same head, regular, arguments by proof irrelevance: true

whnf_core cache: ONE theorem And.intro (use ((f intro).1 = 5) (Eq.refl 5)) (use ((f intro).1 = (f h).1) (Eq.refl _)). The first argument makes the official kernel run the FULL whnf_core on (f intro).1 (step 7 of is_def_eq_core) and cache 5 for it; in the second the cheap whnf_core of (f intro).1 is answered by that cache entry, and 5 against (f h).1 = And.rec .. h is false
twin: the two arguments in the other order (the cache is empty when the projections are compared)
the same with a beta redex instead of mdata: the third argument compares a with (fun x => (f x).1) h, whose value is (f h).1
twin: without the middle argument
